card.keepWhy: A king with a city waiting gave the first minutes to stillness.
sources: Bhagavata Purana 10.70.4 and following (Krishna’s daily routine in Dwarka: he rises at brahma muhurta and meditates on the Self, then bathes, gives gifts and meets his people)
brahma muhurta: the muhurta (about 48 minutes) before the last one of the night, commonly about 96 to 48 minutes before sunrise
check: The film and match say “the hour before sunrise” for brahma muhurta (strictly about 96 to 48 minutes before sunrise); confirm this loose wording is fine.

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? how does your morning usually start? be honest.
options: you’re not alone. listen to this one.
then this king has something for you. listen.

steps.line: Krishna was a king in the golden city of Dwarka: busy, important, surrounded by people who needed him.

steps.q: A king with a whole city waiting for him. How do you think he starts his day?
o: Meeting his ministers, since the city is waiting
Training with his army at dawn
steps.why: Stillness, before anything else. Watch how the Bhagavata tells it.

steps.line: But the Bhagavata Purana describes how he began each day.
Before dawn, in the quiet, he rose and sat in stillness, before anything else.

steps.q: In that stillness, what does the Bhagavata say Krishna meditated on?
o: His plans for the day ahead
His own deepest self, the One
steps.why: Book ten says he meditated on his own self, the one light beyond darkness. Even Krishna, whom devotees see as God, turns inward first.

steps.line: Only then would he bathe, give gifts, greet his people, and start his work.

steps.q: Krishna had more to do than anyone in Dwarka. Why give the first minutes to stillness?
o: The way you start shapes the whole day
Kings were expected to pray at dawn
He was resting up for a long day
steps.why: Krishna wasn’t idle. He had a kingdom to run, and still the quiet came first. The start of the day set the tone for the rest.

steps.line: Hindus call that hour before sunrise brahma muhurta. Many still use it for prayer, or meditation.
steps.label: brahma muhurta

steps.q: A muhurta is an old Indian unit of time. How long is one?
steps.why: Thirty muhurtas make a day. Brahma muhurta is the one that begins about 96 minutes before sunrise.

steps.line: How you start the day shapes the whole day. Even Krishna gave the first minutes to stillness.
steps.label: today

say: here’s what i love. krishna had a whole kingdom waiting, and he still gave the first minutes to stillness.
the bhagavata describes his mornings with love, and many hindus still rise in brahma muhurta, the hour before sunrise, for prayer or meditation.

steps.q: Krishna had a kingdom to run. Why does that make his quiet morning a stronger example than a hermit’s in a cave?
o: A king’s habits carry the force of law
Stillness is for busy people, not just hermits
Dwarka was holier than any cave
steps.why: If a king with a city at his door could find the quiet first, so can someone with a full inbox.

today.say: tomorrow, give the first two minutes to stillness, before your phone. sit and breathe, or say a short prayer, or a name of god. you can watch your breath, learn a prayer, or join in. it’s your choice.
options: good. two minutes of krishna’s morning.
his were full too. two minutes is enough.
